If your fever is above 103°F (39.4°C) or lasts more than three days, seek medical attention.

cold remedies: For common colds, rest, hydration, and over-the-counter meds like acetaminophen or ibuprofen can help.

There is no cure for the cold, but symptoms usually resolve within 7–10 days. Do you have a sore throat or cough?
Zinc lozenges and vitamin C supplements may slightly shorten the duration of a cold.
Avoid antibiotics for colds, as they are viral and not bacterial.
antibiotic use: Antibiotics are only effective against bacterial infections, not viruses like the common cold.
Always complete the full course of antibiotics even if symptoms improve early.
Incorrect use of antibiotics can lead to resistance. Was this prescribed by a doctor?
Do not take leftover antibiotics or share them with others.
Consult a healthcare provider to confirm if an antibiotic is necessary for your condition.
side effects: Common side effects of medications include nausea, drowsiness, or mild rash. What medication are you referring to?
